inputs.share_count_basis: Weighted-average diluted shares, Q1 FY2027 10-Q (quarter ended 2026-07-31), treasury-stock method: 106.8M basic + 0.3M restricted/performance units. Held FLAT because SBC is expensed in the flows. Open-market buybacks have been suspended since the Hostess deal; FY2026 treasury purchases of $5.6M are share withholding on award vesting only, so the flat count is a modelling convention that costs ~0.4% of revenue rather than a funded programme.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2026 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation expense $23.6M, plus $5.6M purchase of treasury shares (shares withheld from stock plan recipients in lieu of cash, financing activities). No combined company figure is published, so the two lines are summed.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. Cost of equity ~8.0% (US 10-year ~4.3% + low-beta staples 0.7 x ~5% ERP); after-tax cost of debt ~3.8% (commercial paper at 4.00%, senior notes ~5% pre-tax); debt is ~32% of enterprise value. That arithmetic gives ~6.6-6.7%. The house rate is set at 7.5%, the same in every scenario: the cushion over the mechanical WACC is the single place where leverage (net debt ~3.3x EBITDA) and the capital-allocation record (roughly $2.9B impaired on a $5.4B acquisition) are charged. Scenario risk is carried by the driver paths and the weights, not by per-scenario discount rates.
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating lease cost stays inside adjusted operating income (rent is expensed in the EBITDA margin), so operating lease liabilities ($159.3M noncurrent at 2026-07-31) are NOT in net debt. Finance leases (~$10M) are immaterial and ignored.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component build, scenario-weighted (dcf-methods routing row 'operating company'). SJM is a US branded consumer-staples manufacturer whose value is a stream of free cash flow; no bank/REIT/holdco features. First valuation of this ticker (fresh build, no reconciliation). | BASE-YEAR CAUTION: FY2026 reported FCF of $1,156M is NOT a mid-cycle base and the forward build does not use it. It is (a) levered, after ~$383M of interest paid, and (b) flattered by income taxes paid of only $42M against $332M in FY2025 and $317M in FY2024 (timing of payments and lower taxable income). The projections are therefore built from components on an UNLEVERED basis with cash tax at ~24.5% of EBIT, and net debt is deducted once in the bridge. | MARGIN DEFINITION: ebitda_margin_path is adjusted operating income (which excludes intangible amortization, impairments, special project costs and unallocated derivative mark-to-market) + depreciation + SBC, as % of net sales. FY2025 ~24.5%, FY2026 ~22.1% (coffee cost/tariff squeeze, Hostess decline), FY2027 guidance implies ~24.4% including the ~$115M IEEPA tariff refund and ~23.1% excluding it. da_pct_path is DEPRECIATION ONLY (~3.2-3.3% of sales): acquired-intangible amortization (~$210-230M/yr) is excluded from both the margin and the tax shield because the big acquisitions were stock deals and the amortization is largely non-deductible; this is the conservative side. | TARIFF REFUND: the ~$115M refund received in Q1 FY2027 is included in year 1 only (it is cash in hand) and remains subject to a DOJ appeal; it is worth under $1/share. | IMPAIRMENTS: the ~$2.9B of Hostess goodwill/trademark write-downs are non-cash and do not enter the flows; they enter as the low Sweet Baked Snacks contribution in the margin path and as the bear scenario. | VINTAGE: balance sheet is 2026-07-31 (Q1 FY2027); Q2 FY2027 results are due around 2026-11-24 and will refresh net debt and guidance. | SBC is ~0.3-0.5% of revenue, so the house/street band is narrow and band_position is of little diagnostic use here.

equity_bridge.item: Pension and other postretirement deficit, after tax
equity_bridge.note: FY2026 10-K: pension funded status -$42.6M, postretirement -$49.2M = -$91.8M pre-tax, tax-effected at ~24%

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR is negative (-7% to -9%) solely because ~$2.9B of Hostess goodwill/trademark impairments and FY2023 pet-divestiture losses were written off book value; it diverges far more than 30 points from revenue growth and is not a usable growth anchor. GAAP EPS was negative in FY2023, FY2025 and FY2026, so EPS CAGRs are undefined. Revenue CAGR (acquisition- and coffee-price-assisted) is used instead, and forward organic growth is set below it.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series = reported FCF less SBC (equity-award withholding is ~$3-8M/yr and only separable from buybacks in FY2025-26): FY2021 $1,229.6M, FY2023 $691.4M, FY2026 $1,127.0M. The 3-year CAGR of 17.7% is an artefact of a depressed FY2023 start (inventory build) and an FY2026 end inflated by $42M of cash taxes; the 5-year figure of -1.7% is the more honest read: owner FCF is no higher than before the Hostess acquisition despite $5.4B spent. Reported and owner FCF CAGRs are near-identical because SBC is tiny. Adjusted EPS (company basis) was $9.15 in FY2026, down 10%.

base.narrative: Guidance year as guided, then a low-growth staples portfolio at a ~23.5% adjusted EBITDA margin.

bull.narrative: Coffee margin holds, Uncrustables and Away From Home compound, Hostess stabilises.

bear.narrative: Coffee pricing rolls over faster than costs, private label and Walmart squeeze margin, Hostess keeps shrinking.

scenario_narratives.base: FY2027 lands on guidance: net sales down ~1.5% (coffee price realisation fading from +22% in FY2026, Sweet Baked Snacks still declining, Uncrustables and Away From Home growing), adjusted operating income of roughly $1.85B including the ~$115M tariff refund. From FY2028 the refund drops out and the margin settles at ~23.2-23.5% adjusted EBITDA, midway between FY2026's squeezed 22.1% and FY2025's 24.5%: coffee earns a normal spread, Transformation Office savings offset Hostess deleverage, and pet stays flat. Revenue grows 1.5-2% on Uncrustables capacity and foodservice against a flat-to-declining centre-of-store base. Capex runs at the guided ~$325M (3.7% of sales), a little above depreciation. Free cash flow of ~$1.3-1.5B unlevered goes to interest, the dividend (~$470M) and debt paydown; the terminal value is capped at 15x unlevered FCF, which binds below the Gordon value.
scenario_narratives.bull: Coffee proves it has durable pricing power: green-coffee costs and tariffs ease faster than shelf prices, volume/mix stays positive (Q1 FY2027 was +2%), and segment profit holds near the Q1 run-rate ex-refund. Uncrustables fills the McCalla capacity and pulls Frozen Handheld and Away From Home to mid-single-digit growth; Hostess stops shrinking after the value-brand divestitures and stabilises at a ~$950M sales base. Adjusted EBITDA margin rebuilds to 25%, above the FY2025 level, and revenue compounds at 2.5-3%. Deleveraging to ~2.5x by FY2029 reopens buybacks. This needs coffee, Uncrustables and Hostess all to cooperate, which is why it carries less than the default bull weight.
scenario_narratives.bear: The FY2027 coffee windfall reverses: as green-coffee prices fall, retailers led by Walmart/Sam's Club (34% of sales, no long-term contracts) force list prices down faster than costs and private label takes share, so coffee dollars and margin both contract. Sweet Baked Snacks keeps declining at high-single digits on GLP-1 adoption and weak snack-cake demand, taking further trademark impairments (non-cash, but a signal), and pet cat food loses distribution. Revenue shrinks for three years and adjusted EBITDA margin falls to 21%, below the FY2026 trough. With net debt at ~3.3x EBITDA, deleveraging stalls and the dividend absorbs most of the free cash flow after interest; equity value is geared to the decline, which is why the bear value falls far more than the EV does. The terminal value does not hit the zero floor: the business stays solidly cash-generative on this path.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 25%: a single customer is 34% of sales with no long-term contracts, net debt of ~$6.7B gears every point of margin into equity value, and FY2027 earnings are partly a coffee-pricing and tariff-refund peak that could unwind. Base held at 50%: guidance was raised in August and the staples categories are defensive. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs three independent things to go right at once (coffee margin durability, Uncrustables capacity fill, a Hostess stabilisation that management has twice failed to deliver).

valuation_philosophy.summary: SJM is valued as a mature, levered, low-growth staples manufacturer on unlevered owner FCF built from components, not on the latest reported FCF: FY2026's $1,156M is post-interest and inflated by a $42M cash-tax year. The discount rate is held at 7.5% in every scenario, above the ~6.6% mechanical WACC, as the one charge for leverage and a poor acquisition record. Because net debt is about a third of enterprise value, the equity is a geared claim: a 2.5-point swing in sustainable EBITDA margin moves the per-share value by roughly 40%. The Hostess impairments are sunk and non-cash; what matters is whether the remaining Sweet Baked Snacks earnings base stabilises and whether the FY2027 coffee margin is a new level or a peak.
key_risks_to_valuation: Leverage gearing: net debt of ~$6.7B against an enterprise value near $20B means small changes in the sustainable margin or the terminal multiple move equity value two to three times as much

FY2027 is a flattering guidance year: ~$115M of tariff refunds (subject to DOJ appeal) plus peak coffee price realisation; the model normalises the margin down 1.2 points in FY2028, and a slower or faster coffee unwind is the main near-term swing

Cash tax normalisation: income taxes paid were $42M in FY2026 against ~$320M in the prior two years; the model assumes ~24.5% of adjusted EBIT in cash, and does not credit any tax shield on intangible amortization
Walmart/Sam's Club at 34% of net sales with no long-term supply contracts
Sweet Baked Snacks: sales down 18% in FY2026, goodwill fully written off, trademark now finite-lived; further decline is in the bear case, not the base
Terminal value is capped (15x base, 17x bull, 12x bear) and the cap binds in all three scenarios, so the valuation is more sensitive to the cap multiple than to terminal growth
Balance sheet is the 2026-07-31 quarter; Q2 FY2027 results due ~2026-11-24 will move net debt and possibly guidance
